title: New York Waterfront Diary
dimensions: 21.6 x 24 cm (trim size; axis order not stated by source)

description.main: Nearly two hundred photographs of New York's changing waterfront by Sophie Fenwick, in mixed formats, with an interview by Pauline Vermare.
description.extended:
A photographic diary of New York's waterfront by the French-American photographer Sophie Fenwick, drawn from an archive built over several decades.

The book holds nearly two hundred images in mixed formats: gelatin silver prints, color slides, stills from Super 8 films and digital snapshots. They show abandonment and decay as well as the waterfront's continuing life, in places such as Coney Island and Red Hook, Brooklyn. Some pictures sit beside poems Fenwick wrote in the early days of the pandemic. The photography curator Pauline Vermare interviews Fenwick, and Lev Zeitlin of Red Square Design made the scrapbook-like layout.

Fenwick was born in New York in 1969 and studied photography at Parsons in Paris and the International Center of Photography. She began photographing the waterfront in the early 1990s while working for Magnum. Her first solo exhibition, Entrepôts d'Eaux (Homage to the Port of New York), was in Paris. This is her first book.
